title: Adaptive FP8 Safety Mesh and Validation for Hopper E4M3/E5M2
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Ship a conservative, observable FP8 activation path for Hopper (E4M3/E5M2) that minimizes customer regressions while unlocking ~20-30% token-cost savings on eligible workloads. This ticket implements a 'safety mesh' — an adaptive set of runtime gates, per-layer drift detectors, and a compact calibration snapshot format — plus a validation harness and canary strategy for rollout.

Scope: calibration runner changes (compact snapshotting, minibatch synthetic calibration), runtime safety gates (telemetry-gated sampling, stochastic rollback), golden-suite accuracy validation, and a canary rollout plan integrated with Console dashboards and automated rollback. Excludes: full INT8 enablement (tracked separately), hardware firmware work.

Motivation and tradeoffs: Full FP8 activation can yield large cost wins but risks subtle accuracy drift on long-tail prompts. We prioritize a conservative, observable rollout: smaller activation surface, more telemetry, and automatic soft-fallbacks. Tradeoffs include slightly higher CPU overhead for per-request drift scoring and retaining small prefix caches for safety checks. These are acceptable to reduce customer-visible regressions.

Design highlights: compact calibration snapshots store per-layer scale + skew estimates with a hash; the runtime can swap snapshots without model reload. Per-layer drift detectors compute a rolling 'drift_score' using prefix logits and calibration residuals; when score > threshold we probabilistically route to FP16/INT8 fallback (stochastic rollback) until score stabilizes. The calibration runner supports seeded synthetic batches for reproducible re-calibration and a golden-seed replay mode for offline validation.

Key metrics to monitor: top-k token distribution KL divergence, pct requests with drift_score > 0.03, eval BLEU/ROUGE/perplexity deltas vs baseline, inference p50/p95 latency impact, and token-cost delta.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration runner can produce compact calibration snapshots and restore them into runtime without full model reload (test: snapshot save/restore in CI)
Safety mesh implements per-layer drift_score and a stochastic rollback that reduces FP8 traffic when drift_score breaches threshold (test: simulated drift injection)
Golden-suite (10k prompt mixes) shows <= 1.5% median metric delta on heldout evals for initial canary cohort and regression alerts fire on breach
Canary rollout automation: ability to route 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automatic pause/rollback based on configurable thresholds in Console
Docs and runbook published with explicit rollback steps and SLOs for latency/cost/quality (runbook link in attachments)
comments: 2025-01-14 - Initial spike complete. Prototype calibration snapshot created (per-layer scale+anchor hash). Observed 18% average token-cost reduction on internal microbenchmarks with Fwd-only workloads.

2025-01-21 - Design review with PM/REVIEW: agreed to add stochastic rollback instead of hard circuit-breaker to reduce flapping for noisy signals. PM (Leah Thompson) requested explicit customer-visible telemetry labels in Console.

2025-01-28 - Engineering sync: implement compact snapshot format (binary + JSON manifest) and snapshot versioning. Telemetry contract v2 drafted (GH PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5583).

2025-02-03 - QA found edge-case: repeated short-chat sessions produced false positives for drift_score due to prefix-length variance. Mitigation: add prefix-length normalization and minimum stability window (10 requests) before stochastic rollback toggles traffic.

2025-02-09 - Canary plan approved by Product. Initial canary cohort limited to internal customers + non-critical public beta. Console dashboard panel (cost/quality/latency) wired to canary route (see attachments).
2025-02-12 - PR opened for runtime gating and snapshot restore (GH PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5621). Needs perf review and security sign-off for snapshot storage format.
2025-02-15 - Ready for internal canary: snapshot restore completes in ~350ms on warm cache, p95 latency increase under 3% in lab. Next: run golden-suite and open pilot with 5 internal tenants.
calibration_steps: 1) Collect representative micro-batches (seeded) from traffic sampling pipeline
2) Run compact calibration runner with per-layer statistics and produce snapshot (include metadata: model hash, input-distribution hash)
3) Run offline golden-suite evaluation comparing snapshot->fp8 outputs vs baseline fp16/float32
4) If metrics within tolerance, stage snapshot to canary pool and enable telemetry gated FP8 route for 5% traffic
5) Monitor drift_score and automated regression alarms for 48h; if breach, increase fallback probability or pause rollout
6) If stable, progress to 25% then 100% following rollout playbook
